name: First Indication of Solar 8B Neutrinos via Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with XENONnT
notes: result_type is "measurement", not "first_detection", "evidence" or "observation": the collaboration's own title says "First Indication" and the paper reports only a 2.73 sigma rejection of the background-only hypothesis, below the conventional ~3 sigma threshold for "evidence". The ontology's result_type enum has no "indication" tier; per the precedent already set in this atlas for an identical situation (result:t2k-electron-neutrino-indication-2011, a 2.5 sigma "indication" paper), the honest choice is "measurement", not the unconstrained "first_detection" type -- "first_detection" reads as an actual detection to a reader and is reserved elsewhere in this atlas (icecube-glashow-resonance-candidate-2021, kamiokande-sn1987a-1987) for events that were actually detected, not a sub-evidence-threshold statistical indication. Corrected during wave-3 independent verification (2026-09-17); the original record mislabeled this as first_detection.

significance.quote: The background-only hypothesis is rejected with a statistical significance of 2.73 sigma.

summary.plain: XENONnT, a dark-matter detector with a 5.9-tonne liquid-xenon target, reported what its title calls a first indication of nuclear recoils from solar 8B neutrinos scattering coherently off xenon nuclei: 37 events were observed above 0.5 keV against 26.4 expected from backgrounds, a 2.73σ rejection of the background-only hypothesis.
summary.technical: Blind analysis, 3.51 tonne-year exposure: 37 events observed above 0.5 keV, (26.4 +1.4/−1.3) expected from backgrounds; the background-only hypothesis is rejected at 2.73σ. Measured 8B solar-neutrino flux (4.7 +3.6/−2.3) × 10⁶ cm⁻² s⁻¹, consistent with results from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory; neutrino flux-weighted CEνNS cross section on Xe (1.1 +0.8/−0.5) × 10⁻³⁹ cm², consistent with the Standard Model prediction. The collaboration's title calls it a 'First Indication'.

title: First Indication of Solar 8B Neutrinos via Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with XENONnT

why_it_matters.locator: arXiv:2408.02877, main text (first page, after the abstract)
why_it_matters.note: The paper's own priority claim, attributed to it; its significance is 2.73σ, below the conventional evidence threshold.
why_it_matters.quote: This is a “first” in three different aspects: the first detection of elastic NRs from astrophysical neutrinos, the first measurement of the CEνNS process with a Xe target, and the first step into the “neutrino fog” by a DM experiment
why_it_matters.value: The paper describes this as a 'first' in three respects: the first detection of elastic nuclear recoils from astrophysical neutrinos, the first measurement of the CEνNS process with a xenon target, and the first step into the 'neutrino fog' by a dark-matter experiment.
